note: Machine-readable known-red set for the full unit suite on this fork, used by local/gate-unit.mjs.
A failure listed here is reported but does not fail the gate; a failure outside it does. Same
shape as local/e2e-known-failure-titles.json, which already gates the scheduled e2e lane.
Every entry names a test title, not a file. A file-level entry (`"test": "*"`) also masks a NEW
failure inside that file, and two of those were found the moment this file was tightened: one
asserted null where the implementation documents undefined, the other linked an `orca` launcher the
fork renamed to `orca-np`. Both were fixed in the tree instead of recorded here.
Two rules: an entry that passes is reported stale and pruned; a named entry nothing matched is
reported unseen, which covers a renamed or deleted case as well as a file that no longer reds.
LOCAL-PATCHES.md stays the evidence for WHY a class is red, not a reason to keep an entry that has
stopped reproducing. Prune wins.
An entry for a file the gate does not run is a problem, not a pass. The gate runs upstream's own
unit lane (`config/scripts/ci-unit-files.mjs` `UNIT_EXCLUDE`), so the 80 files that list drops —
the electron, node-pty, live-shell and cross-version-wire ones — are upstream-quarantined and
deliberately absent here.
A dead entry cannot be reported by the gate at all: staleness is derived only from an entry that
matched a failure, so an entry naming a case upstream deleted would sit here for ever. Every
entry's title is therefore also checked against its own file, statically, by
tests/tools/unit-gate.test.mjs (`titleExistsInSource` in local/unit-gate-judgement.mjs). A title
Vitest only assembles at run time — an `it.each` substitution — is matched with that part as a
wildcard.
An entry may carry a `match` regex, tested against the first line of the failure message. It is
what stops an allowlisted test from covering a NEW failure under the same name: without it the
entry matches on file and title alone, so a passed-in reason stays "known" for as long as the
title does. A `match` is only added where the failure text was observed to carry that signature.

unhandledErrors.headline: Unknown Error: BuildMessage: ModuleNotFound resolving "http://localhost:3000/@fs/Volumes/Storage/.pnpm-store/v11/links/@/monaco-editor/0.55.1/ba98a0706b0d525c508b327ca0c5a44629d435415294976953ca8a51b9cd11ae/node_modules/monaco-editor/esm/vs/language/typescript/ts.worker.js?worker_file&type=module" (entry point)
unhandledErrors.evidence: The browser-mode dev server refuses to serve the Monaco TypeScript worker because this machine's pnpm store lives at `/Volumes/Storage/.pnpm-store`, outside the project directories the dev server is allowed to read. The URL and the store path are the whole finding: no repository file appears in it, and the run it came from had 0 unexpected test failures. A machine whose store sits under the project would not produce it, so it is not a repo red — and not fixable in the fork without loosening `server.fs.allow` for a third-party worker nobody asserts on.
